preconditions.description: The number of nodes (n) and operations (m) are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct nodes within the valid range.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in operations)
preconditions.description: Each operation pair (a_i, b_i) consists of distinct nodes within the valid range.
The input graph is a tree with exactly n-1 edges.

postconditions.expression: len(output) == n and all(0 <= c <= n - 1 for c in output)
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers, each representing a valid count of common elements for each node.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= i <= n and 1 <= j <= n and i != j and (output[i-1] == sum(1 for j in range(1, n+1) if i != j and (set(node_lists[i-1]) & set(node_lists[j-1])))) for i in range(1, n+1))
postconditions.description: For each node i, c_i is the count of nodes j (j ≠ i) such that the lists of node i and node j share at least one common number.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure the `node_lists` data structure is correctly populated according to the operations described in the task.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: The Little Elephant wants to apply m operations. On the i-th operation (1 ≤ i ≤ m) he first adds number i to lists of all nodes of a subtree with the root in node number ai, and then he adds number i to lists of all nodes of the subtree with root in node bi.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure the subtree operations are correctly applied to populate `node_lists` for each node.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: On the i-th operation (1 ≤ i ≤ m) he first adds number i to lists of all nodes of a subtree with the root in node number ai, and then he adds number i to lists of all nodes of the subtree with root in node bi.

candidate_issues.instruction: Replace the expression to correctly reflect that `node_lists` must be derived from the operations on subtrees, not just any arbitrary lists. The expression should ensure that the counts are computed based on the actual lists populated by the operations.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: After applying all operations the Little Elephant wants to count for each node i number ci — the number of integers j (1 ≤ j ≤ n; j ≠ i), such that the lists of the i-th and the j-th nodes contain at least one common number.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure the tree structure is correctly represented (e.g., adjacency list or parent-child relationships) to compute subtrees for operations.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10^5) — the number of the tree nodes and the number of operations. Each of the following n - 1 lines contains two space-separated integers, ui and vi (1 ≤ ui, vi ≤ n, ui ≠ vi), that mean that there is an edge between nodes number ui and vi.
